artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Home Invasion: In Concert at the Royal Albert Hall is a live album and concert film capturing Steven Wilson’s performance at London’s iconic Royal Albert Hall on 29 March 2018, marking the final night of a three-night sold-out residency. Released on 2 November 2018, the album showcases Wilson’s dynamic blend of progressive rock, art rock, and pop sensibilities, drawing from his fifth solo studio album, To The Bone, as well as earlier works with Porcupine Tree and his solo career. The setlist features a career-spanning selection, including tracks like “Pariah,” “Home Invasion / Regret #9,” “The Raven That Refused to Sing,” and “Even Less,” highlighting Wilson’s evolution as a songwriter and his mastery of atmospheric textures, intricate arrangements, and emotive storytelling.

The album stands as a pivotal moment in Wilson’s discography, representing the culmination of a major European tour and the commercial and critical peak of his solo career to date. To The Bone had become his best-selling solo record, and these performances at the Royal Albert Hall were widely regarded as the tour’s crowning achievement. The release was praised for its high production values, immersive sound mix (including 5.1 surround), and visually striking presentation, earning strong reviews for both its musical and technical excellence. Critics lauded the album as a definitive live document of Wilson’s artistry, cementing his reputation as one of progressive rock’s most innovative and compelling figures.
